title: Nimbus Pipeline Solutions
text:
Nimbus Pipeline Solutions

Prospect overview: Nimbus builds an orchestration layer for customer success automation (workflows, agent augmentation, conversation routing). Mid-market, heavy chat/agent workload with large concurrent sessions during business hours.

Why Redwood: migrating from incumbent (OpenAI) after repeated latency regressions on streaming responses and increasing incidence of long tail stalls during tool calls. Nimbus teams reported visible UI freezes for end-users when model streaming slowed >500ms token gaps. They traced to provider-side queuing during peak times; want a more predictable SLO and better streaming consistency.

Recent activity (timeline):
- 2025-01-15: Intro call (Jordan) — discuss high-level architecture, latency targets (median <120ms per token, p95 <400ms for streaming). Prospect notes: "Can't have agents freeze during escalations."
- 2025-01-29: Technical deep-dive w/ Priya — streaming SDK + tool-calling integration discussed. Confirmed webhook architecture for tool calls; need guaranteed ordering for partial responses.
- 2025-02-04: Demo (hosted) — Redwood streaming demo vs incumbent using same prompt set. Nimbus engineer: "Redwood's stream arrived smoother; tail events fewer."
- 2025-02-11: Benchmark planning call, Fireflies ff_2025-02-11_03a9c2 capture. Agreed POC scope: 2-week A/B test with 10k sessions, measure median/p95/p99 streaming latency, token throughput, and error/retry rate.
- 2025-02-18: Pricing call — asked for dedicated capacity pricing for 8x A100-equivalent GPUs and burst policy. Follow-up items listed.

Use-case & requirements (shorthand):
- Workload: low-latency chat agents (real-time streaming), tool calling to external webhooks and internal microservices, multi-tenant routing.
- Latency targets: median per-token <120ms, p95 <400ms for 2k-5k concurrent streams.
- Reliability: graceful fallback to smaller models in case of capacity; deterministic ordering of stream fragments for tool calls.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market; prefers predictable committed pricing (Dedicated) if cost per 1M tokens under threshold.
- Model preferences: open LLaMA-style and curated LLMs; willing to accept quantized variants if quality preserved.

POC details / success metrics (short):
- A/B stream test vs incumbent: measure median/p95/p99 token latency, user-visible stalls, tool-call end-to-end latency.
- Integration: implement Redwood streaming SDK + tool-calling hooks in staging, test ordering guarantees.
- Accept criteria: 30% lower p95 streaming latency vs incumbent OR equal latency with 20% lower cost.

Commercial notes:
- Interested in Dedicated if POC meets SLOs and pricing fits. Requested committed/discount tiers and overage policy.
- Wants SLA language around tail latency for mission-critical paths (CS escalation flows).

Security/compliance:
- Requires SSO (SAML/Okta), audit logs for all model calls, KMS support for key separation. Need data residency clause for EU customer segment (Nimbus serves EU customers via a regional tenant).

Open questions / next steps:
- Redwood to provide staging endpoint, test data schema, and POC runbook by 2025-02-24.
- SE to propose Dedicated pricing for 8x GPUs incl. burst and autoscale caps.
- Legal to confirm SOC2 report availability and add data residency appendix for EU.

Sales cues / quotes:
- "If streaming keeps stalling, our CS NPS drops — we need predictability more than lowest cost." — Head of Product (Nimbus).
- Momentum: technical stakeholders receptive after demo; procurement timeline Q1->Q2 depending on POC.

Internal notes for AE/SE:
- Emphasize streaming stability, tail latency SLA options, and migration assistance (tool-calling examples).
- Prepare a concise benchmark comparison doc (median/p95/p99 charts) against incumbent using Nimbus prompt set.

Potential blockers to close: B2B legal on residency, SOC2 confirmation, final budget sign-off.
